projects.title: Kaleidoscope
projects.subtitle: Different lives, new composition.
projects.alt: Models wearing contrasting patchwork denim jackets.
projects.intro: A pale wash beside a deep indigo. A red panel cutting through familiar blue. Kaleidoscope began with the pleasure of putting those differences together. Discarded denim and factory cutoffs become jackets whose patchwork is meant to be seen, rather than hidden behind a uniform finish.

sections.title: Working with what turns up
sections.text: Recovered denim does not arrive as a perfectly matched roll. There are shifts in colour, wear and thickness. We look for pieces with enough life left in them, then work out how their differences can sit together. A faded section can soften a dark one; a contrasting pocket can change the whole front of a jacket.

sections.title: Patchwork as a design decision
sections.text: We want the eye to travel around the garment. Panels cross the body, colours meet at unexpected points, and the back deserves as much attention as the front. The result should feel composed, even when the material supply is irregular. Cutting and stitching are where that balance has to become real.

sections.title: Made here, with a longer life in mind
sections.text: Kaleidoscope connects our love of expressive dressing with the skill of Kenyan makers. Its purpose is to show that an overlooked material can become a piece someone chooses, wears and keeps. The first collection established the patchwork direction; Collection 002 develops it through curved panels, new pockets and a clearer approach to fit.

projects.title: The Herd
projects.subtitle: A shared identity, an individual presence.
projects.alt: ROHENI cowhide and leather jackets shown on models
projects.intro: We love cowhide for the things a repeat print cannot quite reproduce: the change in hair direction, a dark patch meeting cream, a marking that refuses to land symmetrically. In The Herd, those differences sit alongside leather to give each jacket its own face.

sections.title: Let the markings lead
sections.text: Before a panel is cut, we look at where a marking will fall. A pale area can open up the front of a jacket; a dense dark patch can anchor a shoulder. Leather gives those surfaces a quieter neighbour. The contrast between smooth leather and hair-on hide is part of what makes the pieces feel so physical.

sections.title: A family of individual pieces
sections.text: The Herd is not about making every jacket look the same. Shared shapes and construction connect the pieces, while the available hide changes their character. That is the appeal: a recognisable ROHENI jacket with a surface that belongs to that particular garment.

sections.title: Respect begins before the first cut
sections.text: Because these are animal-derived materials, source and use matter. We work with available cutoffs and overlooked stock, choose panel positions carefully and look for uses for smaller pieces. Recovered material does not make a garment impact-free; keeping clear sourcing records and making well are part of the responsibility.

projects.title: AtIr
projects.subtitle: Cut away, yet still connected.
projects.alt: AtIr black two-piece women’s set with asymmetric cutouts, buckle details and flared sleeves, photographed against orange
projects.intro: AtIr brings a sharper, more sculptural mood to our first collection. A black top and short skirt are held in conversation by sweeping cutouts, buckle details and long, flared sleeves. The spaces between the fabric matter as much as the fabric itself.

sections.title: The shape of confidence
sections.text: The top moves diagonally across the body rather than following a straight line. Its openings expose the construction and interrupt the dark surface; the wide sleeves add volume around a closely shaped waist. The skirt continues that angled movement, giving the two pieces a clear relationship without making them identical.

sections.title: African artistry, in the present tense
sections.text: For us, African artistry includes the freedom of Kenyan makers to experiment. It is in a difficult cut worked through, a fastening placed with care and a familiar fabric made to feel unexpected. AtIr belongs to that living creative practice: made here, expressive on its own terms, ready to be worn wherever its owner takes it.

sections.title: Keeping the material in the story
sections.text: Across ROHENI, we work with factory cutoffs and overlooked materials. AtIr carries the same design intention: make the garment desirable, then let that desire open a conversation about what we choose to value. Its cutouts also remind us that thoughtful cutting must include a plan for the pieces left on the table.

projects.title: Adwoa
projects.subtitle: A set with a presence of its own.
projects.alt: A model wearing the Adwoa top and skirt set from ROHENI’s first collection
projects.intro: Adwoa is the more compact expression of our women’s sets: a coordinated top and skirt, dark surfaces, cutouts and a silhouette that leaves space for the wearer’s own styling.

sections.title: The relationship between two pieces
sections.text: A set asks us to think beyond a single garment. The position of an opening on the top changes how the waist reads; the length of the skirt changes the proportion of the whole look. Adwoa is built around that relationship, while leaving each piece free to be worn separately.

sections.title: Clothes as self-expression
sections.text: We are interested in how someone makes a garment their own: with boots, a bag, a jacket, or the confidence to keep the styling spare. Adwoa expands the first collection beyond outerwear without losing ROHENI’s appetite for contrast and a visible point of view.

sections.title: The same material questions
sections.text: The women’s sets belong to the same studio practice as the patchwork jackets. We ask what an available material can do, which details will make the piece worth keeping and how Kenyan making can be recognised in the finished work. Material choices and construction have to support the look, rather than sit outside its story.

projects.title: Accessories
projects.subtitle: Material character, made to carry.
projects.alt: A cowhide bag from ROHENI’s supplied accessory images
projects.intro: After a jacket is cut, smaller pieces remain. Accessories give us another scale to work at: a striking cowhide marking can become the centre of a bag, while a quiet leather edge frames it. These are everyday objects with the same appetite for texture as the clothes.

sections.title: Small pieces still deserve a good idea
sections.text: A remnant is not automatically a useful product. It still needs a shape, a fastening and a reason to be carried. We look for ways that smaller surfaces can hold their own, balancing expressive markings with the practical demands of a bag or clutch.

sections.title: Something of Nairobi to take with you
sections.text: We want local customers and visitors to encounter African artistry through objects they can use. An accessory offers a small, tangible connection to the studio and the people making here. Its value should be felt in the handling and finishing as much as in the photograph.
